answer: SIM-bound enrollment ties each agent to a paid phone line. First, a newcomer receives a one-time code by SMS, and a carrier lookup against an atlas of number ranges rejects VoIP and bulk prepaid blocks. Second, the hashed number goes on the ledger, so one line backs one identity. Third, each month a random 5% of agents must confirm a fresh code within an hour or lose attesting rights. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 postpaid lines at about $8 each, near $96,000 a year, and no ivory office avoids that bill. Sybils grow like a reef: one polyp at a time, each paying rent.
